title: Your Husband Isn't An Introvert, He Just Doesn't Need Friends
author: Michael Perrone
summary: Michael Perrone argues that male social disengagement isn't introversion--it's the consequence of the disappearance of the male community-building role. In traditional communities, men performed 'kin work' at the frontier: building barns, exploring territory, managing provision--generating social contexts that women then developed into lasting relational connections. Today this frontier is largely gone, filtered through large institutions that strip out the community-building function. Without a frontier to open and without genuine functional need for other men, the modern husband's rational internal calculus is: 'What do I need them for? Everything I do is easier, more comfortable, and more conveniently done without them.' Perrone proposes a new model--'the Local Pillar'--whose three Ps (Prevail, Present, Participate) replace the old Lone Ranger (Protect, Provide, Preside). His examples: a Saturday morning workout group ('Summer of Men') whose male frontier generated unexpected female social connection and father-son initiation; and teenage boys learning dutch-oven cooking who then hosted dinner for teenage girls.
points: * Male social disengagement is not introversion but the disappearance of the male community-building role: opening new social contexts for female kin work to fill is categorically different from participating in female-directed social activities. * In traditional communities, male kin work built the barn; female kin work planned the barn dance--complementary functions where male work expanded the social domain and female work developed it into lasting connection. * The modern male's rational social calculus--'What do I need them for? Everything I do is easier without them'--is functional, not personality-based, reflecting the disappearance of male frontier roles. * Boys grow up without meaningful fraternity because loving, present, engaged fathers are functionally 'dead-beat' socially--modeling manhood with no male community role. * The 'Summer of Men' workout group demonstrates the principle: a male-built frontier produced unexpected female social connection, father-son initiation, and organic (not arranged) community.
quotes: Women are right in thinking men should do their fair share of community building and kin-work, but they're wrong in thinking men should do more of the same work that women are already doing, rather than a community building project that is all their own.
Male kin work uncovers new contexts for social meaning that female kin work then transforms into actual social connection. Male kin work builds the barn. Female kin work plans the barn dance.

What do I need them for? Everything I do, whether it's my job, my hobbies, taking care of my family, my entertainment, relaxing, going on vacation, home repairs, etc. is easier, more comfortable, and more conveniently done without them.
Boys grow up detached from any meaningful fraternity because dad, while being a good, loving, present, and engaged father... is a 'dead-beat' socially.
Our wives have taken this new frontier we found and filled it with more social connection with each other in a way that they didn't have to plan or drag anyone to be a part of.
